evidence_records.notes: TypeSafe introduced Jev as its first public System One model in early access. It describes a new architecture, parallel sampler, and RLCD training; unstructured state enters and typed probabilistic decisions leave. It says Jev gives up string generation and is for structured outputs. These are architecture/product claims, not independently confirmed performance evidence.

evidence_records.source_type: official product and HTTP API documentation
evidence_records.notes: Jev evaluates a text/JSON state against a map of typed questions at POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone. The three question primitives are Choice (selected closed-set option plus per-option probabilities and confidence), Score (ordered-rubric probability-weighted score, probabilities and confidence), and Noul (0–1 yes probability). Questions share state but are evaluated independently and can be mixed in one call.

Current documented version is jev-1.13.0; aliases jev-latest and jev-preview both resolve to it at retrieval. It accepts text only: string, JSON object, or array of text values. Images, audio, and video are unsupported. Context is 64k tokens/request, with a 32k limit for state plus the longest question. English has best documented accuracy; other languages including CJK are accepted but not equally accurate.

Vendor documents current failure modes: literal instruction interpretation, numeric/math and counting unreliability, date/time comparison unreliability, indirection, large irrelevant state, adversarial content, contradictory criteria, some structural invariants, and all generation. It directs users to keep arithmetic/date logic/invariants in code, filter state, give precise criteria, and use generative models for text generation.

Choice and Score confidence is a 0–1 statistic derived from their returned probability distributions; Noul has no separate confidence field. Vendor recommends action thresholds vary by risk and says teams must test/calibrate thresholds on their own domain data. Thus returned confidence is an input to a controlled policy, not evidence an answer is correct.

TypeSafe lists jev-1.13.0 at US$0.042/M input tokens (US$42/B); output tokens are listed as free. Documented limits are 250,000 tokens/sec and 1,200 requests/minute, but TypeSafe says limits are dynamically adjusted and can change without notice. Standard direct access is hosted API, API key, HTTP endpoint, and official Python plus JavaScript/TypeScript SDKs; direct HTTP may be used from any language.

evidence_records.publication_date: 2025-11-19 privacy policy; 2026-04-24 DPA; 2026-08-27 MCA; live docs undated
evidence_records.independence: vendor legal commitments; no external certification evaluated
evidence_records.notes: TypeSafe says it will not train/fine-tune models on Input and will not disclose Input except to service providers; its DPA calls TypeSafe processor for customer personal data and says customer data is retained as necessary. US hosting is stated in the privacy policy. Enterprise ZDR is offered by contact, but no public default retention duration or data-residency choice was found. MCA permits unrestricted processing of Telemetry including logs, hashes, summary statistics, classifications, metrics and learnings; it also says output can be inaccurate and customers must evaluate it independently.

evidence_records.source_type: official live docs and official GitHub organization inventory
evidence_records.publication_date: undated live documentation; organization inventory retrieved 2026-09-18
evidence_records.notes: No official public evidence found for released Jev weights, self-hosting/on-prem deployment, customer fine-tuning/LoRA, or a model card. Docs explicitly say the same weights serve every account and Jev is not fine-tuned or LoRA-adapted with customer data. Public repositories are SDKs, skills and adapters, not Jev weights. Absence of a public page is not proof these options cannot be contracted privately.

Marketing implication of universally reliable automation is limited by the same article: its reported workflow reference answer is an average of two external frontier models, workflows were created by its model-capabilities team, and the vendor says reported 193.6x/444.6x gains are likely high-end real-world gains. It also states 0% type-error is schema matching, not empirical accuracy.

Any claim that no customer-derived data is retained is too broad: the MCA permits telemetry processing without restriction and says TypeSafe has no obligation to retain customer data after termination and may delete it. Direct default retention is therefore not ZDR; enterprise ZDR must be separately obtained/verified.

Four workflow results are equally weighted and measured against model-derived consensus labels: average GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 at high thinking; others use default reasoning. Therefore accuracy is model agreement, not independently adjudicated ground truth. No frozen data, code, raw outputs, denominator, model versions, variance or repeatable run found.

Vendor overview reports67.8%agreement. Independent quality-judge HTML inspection corrected an internal transcription error: four workflow values61.7,71.6,61.8,76.0 have equal-weight mean67.775, rounding67.8. No source arithmetic conflict remains. Metrics remain vendor/model-reference results; not independently reproduced. Report omits aggregate numerical results.

Claims 70–500ms end-to-end response time. Says evals generally ran from US West Coast laptops and a short dense demo state favoured Jev. Schema validity does not validate semantic correctness; OpenRouter LLM data may be biased.

Documents literal reading, unreliable counting/numbers and date comparison, indirection, distractor-heavy context, adversarial content, contradictory criteria and non-guaranteed probability invariants. Advises code for arithmetic/dates and threshold-specific edge-case tests.

evidence_records.independence: independent of TypeSafe; narrow internal study

Labels came from hindsight GPT-5.6 Luna judge plus matcher, not human ground truth. Reports one working profile, Choice ranking regressions, ensemble rate limits and no shipped TypeSafe integration as of Sep 16.

findings.contradiction_check: The same-pool unattended comparison shows no coverage increase; at chat start the narrow-pool Jev configuration covered less than the LLM. The report does not claim universal superiority or an SQE accuracy result.
